title: Smartphone-based extraction-free antioxidant capacity analysis of emulsions by DPPH assay
author: Paraskevopoulou, Tsotsou, et al.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare all required reagents: dissolve N‑acetyl‑l‑cysteine (NAC) to 0.3 % w/v in water; dilute RESVERATROX® 2 % solution 1:1 with ethanol; make a DPPH stock solution of 0.3–0.4 mg/mL in methanol; obtain Grade 1 Chr Cellulose chromatography paper (Whatman).

steps.title: Formulate standard emulsion matrices
steps.instruction: Prepare standard emulsions in the same matrix that will be used for unknowns. For an oil‑in‑water (O/W) matrix combine: Aqua 81.7 % w/w, Paraffinum Liquidum 10 % w/w, Cetearyl Alcohol 4.0 % w/w, Glyceryl Stearate 3.0 % w/w, Phenoxyethanol 1.0 % w/w, Xanthan Gum 0.2 % w/w, Ethylhexylglycerin 0.1 % w/w. For a water‑in‑oil (W/O) matrix combine: Aqua 70 % w/w, Mineral Oil 15 % w/w, Glycerine 5 % w/w, Polyglyceryl‑4 Diisostearate/Polyhydroxystearate/Sebacate 3 % w/w, Microcrystalline Wax 3 % w/w, Polyglyceryl‑3 Diisostearate 2 % w/w, Sodium Chloride 1.5 % w/w, Phenoxyethanol 0.45 % w/w, Ethylhexylglycerin 0.05 % w/w.

steps.title: Dilute unknown samples into matrix
steps.instruction: Dilute each unknown sample into the chosen standard matrix so that the analyte concentration falls within the linear dynamic range; use a dilution factor of at least 100 ×, adding the same amount of water (or other diluent) to the unknowns as was added to the standards to preserve matrix composition.

steps.title: Spot DPPH onto chromatography paper
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, dispense 10 µL of the 0.3–0.4 mg/mL DPPH solution onto a clean strip of chromatography paper; ensure the drop releases freely (no tip‑paper contact) to avoid non‑uniform spreading, then allow the spot to dry completely.

steps.title: Apply emulsion layer on DPPH spot
steps.instruction: With a plastic spatula (never metal), place a 1–2 mm thick layer of the prepared emulsion (standard or diluted unknown) directly onto the dried DPPH spot.

steps.title: Cover and spread emulsion with glass
steps.instruction: Within 10 seconds of applying the emulsion, gently but firmly press a cover glass onto the spot to spread the emulsion into a thin, even layer; scoop any excess that extrudes from the edges with the cover glass and discard it.

steps.title: Incubate and capture images in light box
steps.instruction: Let the prepared strips sit at room temperature for 5–20 minutes. Then place each strip inside a white light box (23 cm × 23 cm, single LED row, Shenzhen PULUZ) and capture a photograph with a 50‑Megapixel smartphone camera (aperture f/1.9, focal length 24 mm, 1× magnification). Position the phone on top of the box with the lens over the opening and keep the strips away from the LED strip to avoid glare.

steps.title: Run assay in duplicate and capture multiple images
steps.instruction: Generate two identical spots per paper strip (duplicate assay). Arrange strips side‑by‑side in the light box, parallel to the LED row, ensuring they are perfectly flat. For each set of samples, acquire at least three photographs within 20 minutes of emulsion application, spacing each capture by at least 5 minutes and always including the calibration standards in the same frame.

steps.title: Analyze images and calculate antioxidant concentration
steps.instruction: Open the images in ImageJ, select a uniform area of each spot (≈ 3500–5000 square pixels) while excluding edge artefacts. Record the Red, Green, and Blue intensity values; choose the channel that gives the best linear fit (typically the Green channel) to construct a calibration curve from the standards. Calculate the unknown concentration from this curve and report the final value as the average of all images that yield a calibration curve with R² ≥ 0.985.
